meta.document_title: Traffic Direction and Control — Standard Operating Procedures
meta.source: Uploaded PDF — Traffic Direction and Control
meta.data_quality_notes: Procedural/operational manual. No fines or citation numbers. Useful for enforcement knowledge base and AI advisor context.

rules.description: Standardized methods of traffic control are more effective and result in improved public relations.

sub_rules.description: For safety and to best observe traffic flow, the center of an intersection is often the best officer position.

When regulating foot traffic or at complex intersections where full manual control is not necessary, the officer should be in the best position to observe approaching traffic. A motorist may fail to obey hand signals if unable to see the officer.

rules.description: Employees will wear a reflective safety vest whenever in the roadway directing or controlling traffic. Wearing the helmet is at the discretion of the officer except when directed by a supervisor. Reflective vests are issued and will be carried at all times.

When hazardous situations develop, a supervisor will direct establishment of a manual traffic control point if needed. For special events, the supervisor may issue directed patrol assignments for manual intersection control. Manual control shall not be used when an existing automatic control device will alleviate the problem.

sections.title: Manual Operation of Traffic Control Devices

rules.description: Manual operation of traffic control signal lights is normally done to recycle a signal or place it on flash. Other situations requiring manual operation include:

sub_rules.description: To facilitate movement at traffic accidents or other emergencies.
To provide uninterrupted movement for a motorcade, funeral procession, etc.
To alleviate congestion resulting from use of automatic controls, particularly during planned special events.

rules.description: When manually operating traffic control signals due to congestion in all four directions, employees will:
procedure_steps: Place the traffic control signal on four-way flash.
Direct traffic from within the intersection until congestion is alleviated.

rules.description: When manually operating due to congestion on one street, employees will:
procedure_steps: Place the traffic signal box switch on 'manual' and run traffic for an extended period in one direction.
Switch to the other direction for shorter periods until congestion is alleviated.

rules.description: It is essential that road users know the officer is present and directing traffic.
Employees will use approved traffic direction and control methods to ensure standardized techniques.
Orders or direction to a motorist or pedestrian should never be vocal except in an emergency. Simple hand signals clearly visible and readily understandable, emphasized by whistle, will conform to:

sub_rules.description: The officer should stand facing one line of stopped traffic with their side toward moving traffic. Any mechanical signals should be turned off if possible, as hand signals combined with traffic signals cause confusion.
The manual 'stop' signal should be given while standing sideways to the flow of traffic, preceded by one blast of the whistle.
sub_sub_rules: Speed and distance should be carefully considered so vehicles can stop safely.
A 'stop' signal will be given when vehicles approach an intersection where cross traffic has right-of-way if there are no other stopped vehicles.

sub_rules.description: The employee maintains arms in the 'stop' signal position and turns at right angles so their side faces the traffic to be started. When clear, the officer turns their head to one direction giving the 'go' signal then to the opposite direction with a similar gesture.
The 'go' signal need not be continuously repeated for a steady stream of vehicles, but vehicles approaching after a gap in traffic flow should be signaled.
One whistle blast is used with the manual 'stop' signal; two blasts with the 'go' signal.
Short rapid whistle blasts warn of unusual or hazardous conditions or to attract attention from persons not responding to hand signals.

rules.description: Vehicles should not be allowed to enter intersections they cannot clear because of congestion immediately beyond.
Advantage should be taken of gaps in one moving line of traffic to stop the flow and start cross traffic moving.
Left turns at an intersection controlled by an officer are at the employee's discretion based on traffic volume and conditions, unless otherwise directed by a supervisor.
Emergency vehicles may have to be directed through an intersection. All vehicular and pedestrian traffic will be stopped for the emergency vehicle to proceed.
If the driver of an emergency vehicle signals a turn, the officer should acknowledge by motioning in the proper direction.
The officer should check to ensure another emergency vehicle is not approaching on a conflicting course. In such circumstance, a very distinct 'stop' signal will be given to one of the vehicles.

If minor traffic violations are observed while directing traffic, they should be overlooked. If the violation is serious, the driver will be instructed to pull clear of the intersection to the nearest curb for proper enforcement action when feasible.
Special contingency plans will be prepared for all planned major special events.
contingency_plan_elements: Entrance and exit of vehicles and pedestrians
Provisions for parking and spectator control
Assignment of point control duties and relief
Temporary traffic controls and parking prohibitions
Appropriate media coverage of such plans

rules.description: No vehicles, including those of volunteer firemen, are allowed to drive into the block where fire apparatus is parked and operating.
No vehicles are allowed to drive over fire hoses without the approval of the on-scene fire commander.
In case of a fire at a facility such as a hospital, no vehicles including volunteer firemen will be allowed on the grounds.
The exceptions to the rules above will be life-saving vehicles on actual calls for service.
Parked vehicles that interfere with fire operations may be towed.
When helicopters land for ambulance service, responsibility for the safety of the helicopter falls on the police department.
The supervisor or on-scene officer will coordinate security of the landing site with the on-scene fire commander.
Alleys and private drives on side streets that may not normally be blocked on an arterial accident are given special consideration.
A safe zone of at least 50 feet should be maintained around the helicopter where no persons will be allowed to enter except emergency personnel.
The Fire Department is responsible for landing and communicating with the helicopter.
The Patrol shift commander will ensure notification is given to any agency or group that may be affected by or needed to help control traffic or road conditions to prevent injury or further damage.
The shift commander may contact news media, Traffic Engineering, Public Works or other departments for assistance.
Supervisors may close roads or streets if existing conditions pose a hazard. If streets may be closed for an extended period, a media release may be prepared to announce the closings.

Temporary traffic control devices will normally only be used with supervisor approval to control traffic during special events or key signal light malfunctions. Cones are located in Patrol cars; barricades or signs may be requested from Public Works. Supervisors will ensure return of all signs when no longer required.
Temporary devices may be used to augment personnel controlling traffic in problem areas or emergency locations arising from severe weather or flooding.
The use of temporary stop signs will be limited to key intersections where a traffic signal has failed completely. Traffic signals placed on four-way flash are preferred over temporary stop signs.
When portable traffic signs are required, employees will request assistance from the Street Department through Communications.
The traffic signal will be placed on four-way flash when temporary signs are in place to avoid confusion.
Employees will ensure that street obstructions and hazards have proper barricades and signs.
If a situation causes a traffic problem or danger, employees will take control of traffic until the necessary barricades are in place.
When a construction company is unable to supply necessary equipment to warn the public, employees will contact the Street Department and request necessary barricades.
